brief: Zero Hedge's prior preview argued August's 162K payrolls print was inflated by an unusually generous seasonal adjustment that would reverse in September, risking a squeeze on CTAs' near-record Treasury shorts. September payrolls printed 29K, below every one of ~80 estimates, with unemployment at 4.2% and August/July revised down a combined 60K. The mechanism: September's seasonal factor subtracted 304K from a 333K raw gain (largest since 2021), mirroring August's rare positive adjustment; BofA ties both to a short four-week survey interval and a late Labor Day. Seasonal adjustment doesn't create or destroy jobs, only shifts it between months, so the two-month drag is close to 2025's. Underlying pace is roughly breakeven per Goldman. The print erased October hike odds and triggered a bond rally (10Y 5.22%→5.16%, Nvidia record) that faded by mid-morning as the household survey showed strength. Fed hiked in September partly on data since revised away.
